category: Acoustics Module I: pressure acoustics interfaces, fluid models, sources and boundary conditions
description: Pressure Acoustics branch of the COMSOL Acoustics Module (6.x): the boundary-mode, asymptotic-scattering and Kirchhoff-Helmholtz interfaces, the frequency-domain, transient and time-explicit (dG) domain models, equivalent-fluid loss models, point/line sources, ports, lumped speaker/port couplings and nonreflecting conditions. Java type strings were taken from the COMSOL 6.4 code-completion data and Application Library models.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Mode (acbm)
tools.description: Solves the Helmholtz eigenvalue problem on a boundary (a duct or waveguide cross section) to find the propagating and evanescent acoustic modes and their out-of-plane wave numbers at a given frequency, the semi-analytical finite element (SAFE) approach. Use it to identify cut-on frequencies and transverse mode shapes of ducts, or to compute numeric mode shapes that are then used as sources in a Port condition. Available for 3D and 2D axisymmetric components; default nodes are Pressure Acoustics, Sound Hard Boundary (Wall) and Initial Values.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Mode; select the inlet/cross-section boundaries; Study > Mode Analysis. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("acbm", "BoundaryModeAcoustics", "geom1")

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries representing the waveguide cross section(s) on which modes are computed.

parameters.name: Azimuthal mode number m
parameters.description: Integer circumferential order used in 2D axisymmetric components (default 0).

parameters.name: Pressure Acoustics node (FluidModel, Poroacoustics, Narrow Region Acoustics)
parameters.description: Fluid model in the cross section; lossy equivalent-fluid models give complex wave numbers.

parameters.name: Mode Analysis study: modeFreq, neigs, shift
parameters.description: Mode analysis frequency, desired number of modes and the out-of-plane wave number to search around.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Variables such as phys_id.vipx/vopx (in-plane/out-of-plane velocity) and aip/aop (acceleration) are defined for postprocessing. For losses in narrow ducts use Thermoviscous Acoustics, Boundary Mode (tabm); with background flow use the Linearized Potential Flow, Euler or Navier-Stokes boundary-mode interfaces.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Asymptotic Scattering (paas)
tools.description: High-frequency scattering interface based on the Kirchhoff-Helmholtz integral with the assumption that the field is locally plane, so the scattered field is written analytically on the surface of an acoustically large object (wavelength much smaller than the object and its radii of curvature). Only the object surface is needed, not a meshed fluid domain, which makes target-strength and scattering studies of submarines or vehicles cheap. Supports spherical and plane incident waves in 3D/2D axisymmetry and plane or cylindrical waves in 2D, includes a visibility factor, and ignores secondary scattering between disconnected objects.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Asymptotic Scattering; default nodes Pressure Acoustics, Background Pressure Field, Scattering Object (with Wall) and Exterior Field Calculation; Study > Frequency Domain. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("paas", "PressureAcousticsAsymptoticScattering", "geom1")

parameters.name: Pressure Acoustics (ExteriorPressureAcousticsModel)
parameters.description: Properties of the infinite exterior fluid (speed of sound, density, attenuation).

parameters.name: Background Pressure Field
parameters.description: Incident plane, spherical or cylindrical wave that illuminates the object.

parameters.name: Scattering Object / Wall
parameters.description: Object surfaces and their reflection properties (sound hard, reflection coefficient, normal impedance, absorption coefficient).

parameters.name: Exterior Field Calculation
parameters.description: Evaluates the scattered far field (paas.efc1.pext, Lp_pext) for target strength plots.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Valid only for open (exterior) problems at high frequency; for low/mid frequencies use Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements (pabe) which captures diffraction and multiple scattering.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Kirchhoff-Helmholtz (pakh)
tools.description: High-frequency radiation interface (also called high-frequency BEM, HFBEM or HFB) that computes the sound radiated by a vibrating object from its surface velocity using the Kirchhoff-Helmholtz integral with a locally-plane-wave assumption, without meshing the surrounding fluid. Valid when the acoustic wavelength is smaller than the structure and its structural modes; for a flat vibrating surface it reduces to the Rayleigh integral. A user-defined option gives access to the full integral by prescribing both surface pressure and normal velocity.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Kirchhoff-Helmholtz; default nodes Pressure Acoustics, Radiating Object (with Wall) and Exterior Field Calculation. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("pakh", "PressureAcousticsKirchhoffHelmholtz", "geom1")

parameters.name: Pressure Acoustics (ExteriorPressureAcousticsModel)
parameters.description: Exterior fluid properties.

parameters.name: Radiating Object / Wall
parameters.description: Surfaces of the radiating body and their source definition (velocity vector, normal velocity or user-defined p and vn).

parameters.name: Exterior Field Calculation
parameters.description: Computes the radiated exterior pressure and SPL (pakh.efc1.pext, pakh.efc1.Lp_pext).

parameters.name: Sound Pressure Level Settings
parameters.description: Reference pressure for SPL; used when a transient solution is transformed with Time to Frequency FFT.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Scattering is not included (the radiating object does not scatter its own field); use pabe or FEM with PML at lower frequencies.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Default domain node (FrequencyPressureAcousticsModel) of Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain that solves the Helmholtz equation and holds the fluid model and model inputs (background temperature and absolute pressure). Fluid models: Linear elastic (density and speed of sound, impedance and wave number, or bulk modulus and density; complex values add losses), User-defined attenuation (Np/m, dB/m or dB per wavelength), Atmosphere attenuation (ANSI S1.26 with humidity), Ocean attenuation, Viscous / Thermally conducting / Thermally conducting and viscous bulk losses, General dissipation (sound diffusivity) and Ideal gas. Porous, narrow-region and anisotropic media use separate domain nodes.
tools.usage: Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Pressure Acoustics 1 (fpam1, default). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").feature("fpam1").set("FluidModel", "AtmosphereAttenuation")

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: FrequencyLinearElastic | Attenuation | AtmosphereAttenuation | OceanAttenuation | Viscous | Thermal | Viscothermal | GeneralDissipation | IdealGas.

parameters.name: LinearElasticOption
parameters.description: crho (density and speed of sound) | Zk (impedance and wave number) | Krho (bulk modulus and density).

parameters.name: c, rho, K_eff, Z, k
parameters.description: Material properties, From material or user defined (complex values allowed).

parameters.name: AttenuationType, alpha1/alpha2/alpha3
parameters.description: neperperm | dBperm | dBperlambda and the attenuation coefficient for user-defined attenuation.

parameters.name: mu, muB, kcond, Cp, gamma, delta_diff
parameters.description: Viscosity, bulk viscosity, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, ratio of specific heats, sound diffusivity for the lossy models.

parameters.name: minput_temperature / minput_pressure
parameters.description: Model inputs T and pA (can be picked up from Heat Transfer or Laminar Flow).

tools.notes: Do not confuse the amplitude attenuation coefficient alpha with the room-acoustics intensity coefficient m = 2*alpha. Gradients in the background pressure (from flow) are not accounted for; use the aeroacoustics interfaces for flow. Dissipation variables acpr.diss_visc, acpr.diss_therm and acpr.diss_tot are available.

tools.name: Poroacoustics (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Domain node that replaces a porous absorber by a homogenized equivalent fluid with complex, frequency-dependent effective density and bulk modulus, so porous liners, foams, fibrous wool, sediments and filters can be included in a pressure acoustics model. Models: Delany-Bazley-Miki (empirical, with Delany-Bazley, Miki, Qunli, Mechel, Komatsu, Allard-Champoux or user constants, air only), Zwikker-Kosten, Attenborough, Wilson, Johnson-Champoux-Allard (JCA), JCA-Lafarge (JCAL), JCA-Pride-Lafarge (JCAPL), three-parameter JCAL approximation (Horoshenkov-Hurrell-Groby), Williams EDFM and Wood. Rigid or limp frame approximations are selectable.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Poroacoustics (pom1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("pom1", "PoroacousticsModel", 3)

parameters.name: FluidModel (Poroacoustics model)
parameters.description: EmpiricalPorous (Delany-Bazley-Miki) | ZwikkerKosten | Attenborough | Wilson | JohnsonChampouxAllard | JohnsonChampouxAllardLafarge | JohnsonChampouxAllardPrideLafarge | HoroshenkovHurrellGroby | Williams | Wood.

parameters.name: Constants
parameters.description: DelanyBazley | Miki | Qunli | MechelGlassFiberLowX/HighX | MechelRockFiberLowX/HighX | Komatsu | AllardChampoux | UserDefined (C1..C8) for the empirical model.

parameters.name: Rf, epsilon_p, tau, Lv, Lth
parameters.description: Flow resistivity, porosity, tortuosity factor, viscous and thermal characteristic lengths.

parameters.name: kp0_th, tau0, taup0_th
parameters.description: Static thermal permeability and static tortuosities for JCAL/JCAPL.

parameters.name: PorousApproximation, rhod
parameters.description: Rigid | Limp frame; drained density of the porous matrix for the limp model.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Delany-Bazley-Miki is valid only for air and porosity close to 1. When the elastic skeleton matters (heavy foams, poroelastic layers bonded to plates) use the Poroelastic Waves interface; for anisotropic absorbers use Anisotropic Poroacoustics. Other examples: porous_absorber, porous_material_characterization.

tools.name: Narrow Region Acoustics (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Equivalent-fluid domain model that smears the viscous and thermal boundary-layer losses of narrow channels of constant (or slowly varying) cross section onto the fluid, at a fraction of the cost of a Thermoviscous Acoustics model. Accurate for long tubes and slits (length much larger than the radius), applicable to gases and liquids, and valid also when the boundary layers overlap. Impedance-jump (end) losses at cross-section changes are not captured.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Narrow Region Acoustics (nra1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("nra1", "NarrowRegionAcousticsModel", 3)

parameters.name: DuctType
parameters.description: WideDuct (wide duct approximation) | NarrowDuct (very narrow circular duct, isothermal) | Slit | CircularDuct | RectangularDuct | EquilateralTriangularDuct | UserDefinedDuctType.

parameters.name: a, h, a_rect, b_rect, d_tri, Hd
parameters.description: Radius, slit height, rectangle sides, triangle side length or hydraulic diameter of the duct.

parameters.name: mu, kcond, Cp, gamma, c, rho
parameters.description: Fluid properties (default From material).

parameters.name: nterms
parameters.description: Number of terms in the series solution for the rectangular duct.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. For waveguides of varying thickness or curved walls use the Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance condition; for short ducts with end losses or complex geometry use Thermoviscous Acoustics. Also used in loudspeaker_driver, lumped_receiver_04cc and helmholtz_resonator_with_flow.

tools.name: Anisotropic Acoustics (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Domain node that models a fluid with an effective anisotropic density tensor and an effective bulk modulus, solving a generalized Helmholtz equation with rho^-1 as a tensor. Used for homogenized acoustic metamaterials (cloaks, lenses) and fibrous materials with direction-dependent properties; principal sound speeds follow from the eigenvalues of c^2 = rho^-1*K. Available in the frequency-domain and transient pressure acoustics interfaces.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain (or Transient) > Anisotropic Acoustics (aam1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("aam1", "AnisotropicAcousticsModel", 2)

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Coordinate system in which the density tensor is given (default Global; must not rotate in time).

parameters.name: K_eff
parameters.description: Effective bulk modulus (Pa), From material or user defined.

parameters.name: rho (Isotropic | Diagonal | Symmetric)
parameters.description: Effective density tensor representation and values.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Use a cylindrical/curvilinear coordinate system for radially graded cloaks. For anisotropic porous absorbers use Anisotropic Poroacoustics.

tools.name: Anisotropic Poroacoustics (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Equivalent-fluid model for porous materials with direction-dependent flow resistivity, tortuosity and viscous characteristic length, producing an anisotropic effective density tensor and a scalar bulk modulus. Three models are available: Johnson-Champoux-Allard (default), JCA-Lafarge and JCA-Pride-Lafarge, with rigid or limp frame. Typical uses are fibrous or layered absorbers whose properties differ in-plane and through the thickness.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Anisotropic Poroacoustics (apm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("apm1", "AnisotropicPoroacousticsModel", 3)

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: JohnsonChampouxAllard | JohnsonChampouxAllardLafarge | JohnsonChampouxAllardPrideLafarge.

parameters.name: Rf, tau, Lv (tensors)
parameters.description: Anisotropic flow resistivity, tortuosity factor and viscous characteristic length.

parameters.name: epsilon_p, Lth, kp0_th
parameters.description: Porosity, thermal characteristic length and static thermal permeability (scalars).

parameters.name: coordinateSystem, PorousApproximation
parameters.description: Local material axes; Rigid or Limp frame.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. For an elastic anisotropic skeleton use Anisotropic Poroelastic Material in the Poroelastic Waves interface.

tools.name: Monopole Domain Source (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Adds a user-defined monopole volume source term Qm (1/s^2) to the right-hand side of the Helmholtz or scalar wave equation; the source radiates equally in all directions. Use it for custom distributed sources, a heat-release driven pressure source written by hand, or user-defined nonlinear contributions in the time domain. Dedicated monopole-type sources exist as Heat Source, Flame Model and (transient) Westervelt contributions.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > More > Monopole Domain Source (ms1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("ms1", "MonopoleSource", 3)

parameters.name: Qm
parameters.description: Monopole domain source (SI unit 1/s^2); any expression, e.g. a Gaussian spatial distribution.

tools.notes: Available in Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain / Transient / Boundary Mode and in the SLNS interface. The Java property name Qm is inferred from the GUI symbol and not listed in the completion data; check with model.component(...).physics("acpr").feature("ms1").properties().

tools.name: Dipole Domain Source (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Adds a dipole domain source qd (N/m^3), a volumetric force density, to the pressure acoustics equation; the resulting source radiates preferentially in two opposite directions. Useful for distributed force-type sources and for advanced user-defined contributions, for example approximate convection by a uniform flow. In 2D axisymmetry the r-component should normally be zero.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > More > Dipole Domain Source (ds1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("ds1", "DipoleSource", 3)

parameters.name: qd
parameters.description: Components of the dipole domain source vector (N/m^3).

tools.notes: Property name qd follows the GUI symbol (verify with properties()). In the time-explicit interfaces the equivalent is the Volume Force Source.

tools.name: Heat Source (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Domain heat source that generates sound by rapid thermal expansion and contraction of the fluid, for example a pulsating laser beam (photoacoustics). It adds a monopole source proportional to the heat source strength times the isobaric thermal expansion coefficient, computed from c, Cp, gamma and the model-input temperature. For flames in combustion instability studies use the Flame Model.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > More > Heat Source (hts1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("hts1", "HeatSource", 3)

parameters.name: Q_heat
parameters.description: Heat source strength (W/m^3).

parameters.name: Cp, gamma
parameters.description: Heat capacity at constant pressure and ratio of specific heats (From material or user defined).

parameters.name: Model input T
parameters.description: Ambient temperature, always shown, used for the thermal expansion coefficient.

tools.notes: The Time Explicit and Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit interfaces have their own Heat Source feature (HeatSource, tag hs).

tools.name: Aeroacoustic Flow Source (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: 3D domain feature that sets up flow-induced noise sources (Lighthill analogy or the aeroacoustic wave equation) in pressure acoustics from a scale-resolving CFD solution (LES, DES or RANS SST-SAS) or imported CGNS flow data. It is used in the hybrid computational aeroacoustics (CAA) workflow together with the Aeroacoustic Flow Source Coupling and the Transient Mapping study, followed by a Time to Frequency FFT. Without the coupling, the Lighthill stress tensor T, the exterior normal mass flow and the second time derivative of the flow pressure can be given as user-defined Fourier components.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > More > Aeroacoustic Flow Source (afs1), 3D only. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("afs1", "AeroacousticFlowSource", 3)

parameters.name: AcousticAnalogy
parameters.description: Lighthill | LighthillApproximate (aeroacoustic wave equation).

parameters.name: T, mn, pvartt
parameters.description: Stress tensor, normal mass flow on exterior boundaries and flow pressure second time derivative (coupled automatically when the multiphysics coupling is used).

parameters.name: useWindowFunction, window
parameters.description: Window function to truncate a compact source region consistently.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (and the CFD Module for LES/DES flow). See the user's guide chapter 'Modeling with the Aeroacoustic Flow Source: Flow-Induced Noise' for the setup sequence.

tools.name: Flame Model (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Heat-release source based on the n-tau model for thermoacoustic (combustion) stability analysis: the heat release in the flame region at time t is coupled to the acoustic velocity at a reference point or boundary at t - tau_u. It adds a monopole source to the Helmholtz equation, and an Eigenfrequency study then shows whether modes of a combustor are amplified or damped. Parameters are the interaction index, time lag, steady heat release and steady flow speed.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > More > Flame Model (flm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("flm1", "FlameModel", 3)

parameters.name: n_u, tau_u
parameters.description: Interaction index and time lag of the n-tau model.

parameters.name: Q_s, U_s
parameters.description: Steady heat release (W/m^3) and steady flow speed (m/s).

parameters.name: acoRef, N_ref, referenceSource
parameters.description: Acoustic reference: refPoint | refBoundary and the reference vector (automatic or user defined).

parameters.name: Cp, gamma
parameters.description: Fluid properties used for the thermal expansion coefficient.

tools.notes: Because the source depends on frequency through exp(-i*omega*tau), the eigenvalue problem is nonlinear; COMSOL linearizes it automatically. Negative imaginary parts of the eigenfrequency indicate growing (unstable) modes with the +i*omega convention.

tools.name: Pressure (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Boundary condition that prescribes the total acoustic pressure p_t = p0 on a boundary, acting as a pressure source (in the frequency domain p0 is the harmonic amplitude). It is the classic way to drive a tube, horn throat or resonator with a known pressure, and the pair version applies it between assembly parts. The Pressure (point condition) variant constrains the pressure at points.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Pressure (pr1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("pr1", "Pressure", 2)

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Prescribed pressure amplitude (Pa).

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Pointwise/weak constraint options under Advanced Physics Options.

tools.notes: A pressure condition fully reflects waves coming back to it; for an absorbing source use a Port, Plane Wave Radiation with Incident Pressure Field, or a Lumped Port.

tools.name: Matched Boundary (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Nonreflecting boundary condition that lets one mode (wave number k1) or two modes (k1 and k2) leave a duct or waveguide with minimal reflection, optionally with an Incident Pressure Field subnode. It is useful in ducts below the cut-off of the second excited transverse mode: set k1 = omega/c and k2 = omega1/c where omega1 is the cut-off of the first excited mode (found with a Boundary Mode model). With k1 = k2 = omega/c it reduces to the plane wave radiation condition.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Matched Boundary (mb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("mb1", "Matched", 2)

parameters.name: MatchedOption
parameters.description: K1Option (one mode, default) | K1K2Option (two modes).

parameters.name: k1, k2
parameters.description: Wave numbers (rad/m) of the matched modes.

tools.notes: If several modes propagate use Port conditions (one per mode) instead.

tools.name: Perfectly Matched Boundary (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: A perfectly matched layer applied directly on an open outer boundary without drawing a layer domain: the PML is built automatically with COMSOL's extra-dimension machinery. It absorbs all wave types, including oblique and non-plane waves, and is the most convenient truncation for radiation and scattering problems in Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain (the only interface that has it). Settings mirror a classical PML: attenuation direction, stretching type and number of mesh points through the virtual layer.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Perfectly Matched Boundary (pmb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("pmb1", "PerfectlyMatchedBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: directionType, r0, cdir
parameters.description: Attenuation direction radial (center r0) | normal | custom (direction cdir).

parameters.name: stretchingType
parameters.description: logarithmic | polynomial (default) | rational | userDefined.

parameters.name: scaleFactor_p/_r/_l, gamma_p/_r/_l
parameters.description: PML scaling factor and curvature (or real-term) parameters per stretching type.

parameters.name: TypicalWavelength, lamref
parameters.description: Automatic or user-defined typical wavelength.

parameters.name: numelem_p/_r/_l, isUniform
parameters.description: Number of mesh points in the virtual layer; uniform thickness option.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Place an Exterior Field Calculation surface inside the physical domain for far-field results. For other interfaces (thermoviscous, aeroacoustics, transient) use a Perfectly Matched Layer domain under Definitions.

tools.name: Incident Pressure Field (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Subnode of Plane, Spherical and Cylindrical Wave Radiation and Matched Boundary that injects an incoming wave through a nonreflecting boundary while still absorbing outgoing waves. Field types are plane wave, cylindrical wave, spherical wave or user defined; a plane-wave expansion option allows plane-wave incidence in 2D axisymmetric models. Optional calculation of incident and reflected intensity gives absorption and transmission directly; the incident field on the boundary is available as acpr.p_i.
tools.usage: Right-click Plane Wave Radiation (or Spherical/Cylindrical Wave Radiation, Matched Boundary) > Incident Pressure Field (ipf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").feature("pwr1").create("ipf1", "IncidentPressureField", 2)

parameters.name: PressureFieldType
parameters.description: Plane wave (default) | Cylindrical wave | Spherical wave | User defined.

parameters.name: pamp (p0), c, dir (ek), phi
parameters.description: Amplitude, speed of sound, wave direction and phase of the incident wave.

parameters.name: CalculateIntensity, rho
parameters.description: Compute incident and reflected field intensity at the boundary (needs the density).

tools.notes: Never apply an incident field on the outer boundary of a PML. Pressure Acoustics, Transient has the same subnode with time-domain settings.

tools.name: Port Reference Axis (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Subnode of the acoustic Port that defines the azimuthal reference direction of circular and annular port modes by selecting two points in the geometry. It is required when the Port type is Circular or Annular so that non-axisymmetric modes (m > 0) have a well-defined orientation, which matters when several ports must be consistent, e.g. inlet and outlets of a muffler.
tools.usage: Right-click Port (Circular or Annular type) > Port Reference Axis (cpra1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").feature("port1").create("cpra1", "CircularPortReferenceAxis", 0)

parameters.name: Point selection
parameters.description: Two points defining the azimuthal reference axis of the port.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module.

tools.name: Periodic Port (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Port for periodic structures (absorbers, diffusers, metasurfaces) that handles plane-wave incidence at a given polar angle together with all reflected and transmitted diffraction orders, splitting reflected energy into specular and non-specular directions. It is combined with a Periodic Condition of Floquet type whose k-vector points to the periodic port; one port gives a reflection problem, two parallel ports a transmission problem. Diffraction Order Port subnodes capture the individual orders.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Periodic Port (pport1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("pport1", "PeriodicPort", 1)

parameters.name: PortExcitation, IncidentWave
parameters.description: Incident wave excitation on/off; defined by Amplitude (pamp) or PowerPerLength (P0).

parameters.name: thetai, phi
parameters.description: Polar angle of incidence and phase.

parameters.name: IncidentPeriodicPort
parameters.description: On the second (transmission) port: take mode settings from the incident periodic port.

tools.notes: Check that enough diffraction orders are included by evaluating imag(acpr.pport1.dport1.kn), imag(acpr.pport1.dport2.kn), ... in a Global Evaluation: orders with zero imaginary part propagate and must have a Diffraction Order Port. Also used in porous_absorber.

tools.name: Diffraction Order Port (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Subnode of the Periodic Port that absorbs and quantifies one diffraction order (m in 2D, m and n in 3D) scattered by a periodic structure. Orders are typically added in positive/negative pairs of the same order; each gives its own reflection or transmission coefficient so that specular and diffuse reflection can be separated, e.g. for diffuser scattering coefficients.
tools.usage: Right-click Periodic Port > Diffraction Order Port (dport1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").feature("pport1").create("dport1", "DiffractionOrderPort", 1)

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Diffraction order (integer, positive or negative).

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Second diffraction order index in 3D models.

tools.notes: Propagating orders have real kn; evanescent orders need not be included.

tools.name: Lumped Port (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Couples the end of a waveguide (plane-wave region) to an exterior system with a lumped representation: an Electrical Circuit (electroacoustic transducer), a two-port transfer matrix (acoustic or electroacoustic), or a lumped waveguide. The exterior condition can be a circuit, an ideal pressure/volume-flow or voltage/current source, a lumped impedance (user, RCL or end impedance) or a port, so receivers, microphones and ducts can be reduced to lumped elements. Variables acpr.lport1.p1/p2 and Lp1/Lp2 give pressure and SPL at both ends of a two-port.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Lumped Port (lport1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("lport1", "LumpedPort", 2)

parameters.name: ConnectionType
parameters.description: Circuit | TwoPort (default) | Waveguide.

parameters.name: TwoPortRepresentation, T11_a..T22_a / T11_ea_in..
parameters.description: Acoustic or electroacoustic transfer-matrix elements of the two-port.

parameters.name: ExteriorCondition
parameters.description: Circuit | IdealSource | Impedance | Port.

parameters.name: AcousticInputSource / ElectroacousticInputSource
parameters.description: Pressure | VolumeFlow, or Voltage | Current, with pav_in, Q_in, V_in, I_in.

parameters.name: ImpedanceModel, RCLModel, EndImpedanceType
parameters.description: UserDefined | RCL | EndImpedance terminations (flanged/unflanged pipe).

parameters.name: PortArea, MultiplicationFactor, A_scale
parameters.description: Port area with symmetry handling.

tools.notes: Place the port at least one duct diameter away from geometry features so only a plane wave exists. Also used in full_ear_hearing_aid and lumped_receiver_vibroacoustic; a thermoviscous version exists (ta, slns).

tools.name: Lumped Speaker Boundary (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Models a loudspeaker driver (cone, dust cap, surround and motor) as a piston boundary coupled to an Electrical Circuit that carries its Thiele-Small lumped model, applied on the diaphragm surface with the driver equivalent area. The back volume can be lumped as a compliance, an RCL circuit or a user-defined impedance, or disabled when both sides are modeled. It is a low-frequency (piston) approximation ideal for early design, cabin/room placement studies and driver comparisons.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Lumped Speaker Boundary (lsb1); add an Electrical Circuit with an External I vs. U node. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("lsb1", "LumpedSpeakerBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: I_cir
parameters.description: Input current from the External I vs. U circuit node.

parameters.name: BackVolumeAcousticImpedance, V_back
parameters.description: VolumeCompliance | RCL | UserDefined | NoCorrection and the back volume.

parameters.name: Rac, Lac, Cac, Zac
parameters.description: Equivalent acoustic resistance, inertance, compliance or impedance of the back volume.

parameters.name: SpeakerAxisDirection, e_ax, ReverseAutomaticDirection
parameters.description: Speaker axis (automatic or user defined).

parameters.name: SpeakerArea, MultiplicationFactor, A_scale
parameters.description: Area and symmetry scaling.

tools.notes: Does not capture cone break-up; use a full vibroacoustic driver model (loudspeaker_driver) at high frequency. If the diaphragm is an interior boundary use Interior Lumped Speaker Boundary; the front-radiated power is available as acpr.lsb1.P_front.

tools.name: Interior Lumped Speaker Boundary (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Interior-boundary version of the Lumped Speaker Boundary for a diaphragm modeled as a shell with air on both sides: the lumped Thiele-Small driver in an Electrical Circuit is driven by the pressure difference across the boundary and imposes a piston velocity. Used for loudspeakers in enclosures, headphones on artificial ears and microspeakers where the front and back cavities are both meshed.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Lumped Speaker Boundary (ilsb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("ilsb1", "InteriorLumpedSpeakerBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: I_cir
parameters.description: Input current linked to the circuit External I vs. U node.

parameters.name: ReverseAutomaticDirection
parameters.description: Reverse the automatic speaker axis direction (acpr.ilsb1.e_axx/e_axy/e_axz).

parameters.name: MultiplicationFactor, A_scale
parameters.description: Speaker area scaling for symmetry.

tools.notes: Also available in Pressure Acoustics, Transient (lumped_loudspeaker_driver_transient) and in Thermoviscous Acoustics for microtransducers.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Boundary condition (the BLI model) that adds viscous and thermal boundary-layer losses at walls in a pressure acoustics model by integrating the boundary layers analytically, giving thermoviscous accuracy at pressure-acoustics cost. It works for arbitrary geometry as long as boundary layers do not overlap (not in extremely narrow gaps or very sharp curvature), and supports moving walls through velocity sources and temperature-variation sources. Wall thermal conditions include isothermal, adiabatic, temperature variation and a thermally conductive finite or infinite wall.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance (tvb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("tvb1", "ThermoviscousBoundaryLayerImpedance", 2)

parameters.name: MechanicalCondition
parameters.description: NoSlip | Slip | Velocity | NormalVelocity (with vel or nvel sources).

parameters.name: ThermalCondition
parameters.description: Isothermal | Adiabatic | TemperatureVariation (Tbnd) | ThermallyConductiveWall.

parameters.name: WallType, d, rho_w, Cp_w, kcond_w, BacksideWallCondition
parameters.description: Finite or infinite conductive wall properties.

parameters.name: mu, kcond, Cp, gamma, c, rho
parameters.description: Fluid properties (From material).

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. With vibrating structures, the multiphysics subfeature of Acoustic-Structure Boundary (Thermoviscous Boundary Layer Impedance, CouplingThermoviscousBoundaryLayerImpedance) supplies the wall velocity. Mesh the wall with enough resolution of the tangential pressure gradient.

tools.name: Transfer Matrix Coupling (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Couples a source and a destination boundary through a transfer-matrix representation of the omitted component, such as a diesel particulate filter, a lumped structure or an acoustic subsystem. The pointwise option couples pressure and velocity at every point of identical (possibly rotated) boundaries; the lumped two-port option couples the average pressure and volume flow of boundaries of any shape, assuming plane waves. Matrix entries T11..T22 can be analytical, interpolated data or frequency dependent.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Transfer Matrix Coupling (tmc1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("tmc1", "TransferMatrixCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: Representation
parameters.description: TransferMatrix (pointwise, default) | TransferMatrixLumped (lumped two-port).

parameters.name: T11, T12, T21, T22 (pointwise) / T11_l..T22_l (lumped)
parameters.description: Complex transfer-matrix components, typically functions of freq.

parameters.name: Area, MultiplicationFactor, A_scale
parameters.description: Source/destination area handling for the lumped option.

parameters.name: TransformationMethod, meshSimilarity
parameters.description: Mapping between the source and destination boundaries for the pointwise option.

tools.notes: The transfer matrix of a subsystem can itself be computed with two Ports (acpr.T11..T22 are generated automatically when a model has exactly two plane-wave ports).

tools.name: Interior Impedance / Pair Impedance (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Transfer-impedance condition on an interior boundary (or between the parts of an assembly pair) relating the pressure jump across it to the normal particle velocity, generalizing sound-hard and sound-soft conditions. Built-in models represent a perforated plate, a thin elastic plate, a membrane or a porous mass layer (e.g. a thin fabric or felt), and a user-defined specific transfer impedance Zn can include resistance and reactance data.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Impedance (iimp1), or Pairs > Pair Impedance. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("iimp1", "InteriorImpedance", 2)

parameters.name: ImpedanceModel
parameters.description: UserDefined | PerforatedPlate | Membrane | PorousMassLayer (thin plate available in the GUI list).

parameters.name: Zn
parameters.description: Specific transfer impedance (Pa*s/m) for the user-defined option.

parameters.name: tp, E, nu, rhol, eta_s
parameters.description: Thickness, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, density and loss factor for plate/membrane models.

parameters.name: Rf, flowRes
parameters.description: Flow resistivity or flow resistance for the porous mass layer.

parameters.name: WaveDirection, thetai, ci
parameters.description: Direction/angle of the incident wave for angle-dependent models.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module for the built-in models. For perforates with thick/thin plate theory and nonlinear high-SPL terms the dedicated Interior Perforated Plate feature has more options. Pair versions use src/dst instead of up/down.

tools.name: Interior Perforated Plate / Pair Perforated Plate (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition that represents a perforated plate by its transfer impedance computed from hole diameter, plate thickness and area porosity, avoiding meshing thousands of holes. Model types are Thin plate (thermal losses negligible), Thick plate (includes thermal effects) and the legacy asymptotic model; end corrections, hole-hole interaction (Fok function), user-defined resistance/reactance and nonlinear high-amplitude terms with discharge coefficients can be added.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Perforated Plate (ipp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("ipp1", "InteriorPerforatedPlate", 2)

parameters.name: PerforatedPlateType
parameters.description: ThinPlate (default) | ThickPlate | OldModel (asymptotic legacy).

parameters.name: dh, tp, porArea
parameters.description: Hole diameter (default 1 mm), plate thickness (1.5 mm) and area porosity (0.1).

parameters.name: EndCorrectionType, delta_re, delta_im
parameters.description: BuiltIn (4*dh/(3*pi)) or user-defined end corrections.

parameters.name: HoleInteractionType, f_int
parameters.description: FokFunction or user-defined hole-hole interaction.

parameters.name: IncludeNonlinearEffects, C_lin, C_nl, f_nl
parameters.description: Nonlinear (velocity-dependent) resistance terms.

parameters.name: IncludeUserDefinedTerms, theta, chi
parameters.description: Additional user-defined resistance and reactance.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Also used for seat/cabin trim in car_cabin_acoustics and the grill in headphone_artificial_ear. With grazing mean flow use the aeroacoustics interfaces' Interior Impedance.

tools.name: Interior Sound Hard Boundary (Wall) (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Zero normal velocity condition on an interior boundary with a pressure discontinuity (slit) across it, representing an infinitely thin rigid wall inside an acoustic domain such as baffles, thin partitions, fins of a diffuser or the walls of a thin tube. It avoids having to draw and mesh a thin solid. Available in the frequency-domain, transient, boundary-element and time-explicit pressure acoustics interfaces.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Sound Hard Boundary (Wall) (ishb1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("ishb1", "InteriorSoundHard", 2)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Interior boundaries only; no further settings.

tools.notes: Pressure and SPL jump across the boundary; use up()/down() operators to evaluate each side.

tools.name: Interior Normal Acceleration / Velocity / Displacement (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Source conditions on interior boundaries that prescribe the normal acceleration, velocity or displacement of an infinitely thin moving surface while allowing a pressure discontinuity across it. Typical uses are a loudspeaker cone or membrane represented as a boundary inside the air domain, or imposing a known structural vibration on an embedded surface. Each can be given as a full vector (normal part taken) or as an inward normal component.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Normal Acceleration (ina1) / Interior Normal Velocity (inv1) / Interior Normal Displacement (ind1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("ina1", "InteriorNormalAcceleration", 2)

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Acceleration (vector acc) or Normal acceleration (a_n); similarly Velocity/Normal velocity or Displacement/Normal displacement.

parameters.name: acc / a_n
parameters.description: Acceleration vector (m/s^2) or normal acceleration; normal points outward (shown as a red arrow).

tools.notes: For exterior boundaries use Normal Acceleration/Velocity/Displacement. When the moving surface is computed by a shell or solid, use the Acoustic-Structure Boundary coupling instead.

tools.name: AWE Expression (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Defines the response metric used by the asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) in an Adaptive Frequency Sweep, so that the physics-controlled AWE expression setting works. The metric can be a user-defined global expression (e.g. an averaged SPL), a point integration giving the summed |p|^2 at selected probe points, or a port scattering coefficient when Port features exist. A well-chosen metric lets the fast AWE solver resolve sharp resonances with far fewer solves than a regular sweep.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Variables > AWE Expression (awee1); Study > Adaptive Frequency Sweep with AWE expression type = Physics controlled. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("awee1", "AsymptoticWaveformEvaluationExpression", -1)

parameters.name: AWE_src
parameters.description: userdef (default) | PointIntegration | a Port AWE expression when ports exist.

parameters.name: AWE
parameters.description: User-defined global AWE expression, e.g. aveop1(acpr.Lp_t).

parameters.name: Point Selection
parameters.description: Probe points used by the Point integration option.

tools.notes: The global-feature dimension (-1) in the Java create call is an assumption for a physics-level global node; confirm by recording the action in the GUI (File > Save as Java). With awefunctype = usercontrolled, enter the expressions in the study step (awefunc) instead.

tools.name: Quadrupole Point Source (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Point source made of two closely spaced opposite dipoles, used together with monopoles and dipoles to approximate complex sources through a multipole expansion (e.g. jet or rotor noise, vibrating small bodies). Predefined types are Power (longitudinal), where the D and d vectors are parallel, and Power (lateral), where they are perpendicular; a user-defined option takes the D and d vectors directly. In 2D axisymmetry it is placed on the axis and only longitudinal orientation is possible.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Points > Quadrupole Point Source (qps1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("qps1", "FrequencyQuadrupolePointSource", 0)

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: PowerLongitudinal (default) | PowerLateral | UserDefined.

parameters.name: P_rms
parameters.description: Free-space reference power (RMS) for the power types.

parameters.name: dir, n
parameters.description: Quadrupole direction and lateral quadrupole normal.

parameters.name: D, d, phi
parameters.description: Quadrupole D-vector (N), d-vector (m) and phase for the user-defined type.

tools.notes: Point sources create a singular field at the point; evaluate the field some distance away and refine the mesh around the source. In 2D components the equivalent is FrequencyQuadrupoleLineSource (an infinite line source).

tools.name: Line Source (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Source on an edge in 3D components, equivalent to a radially pulsating cylinder of vanishing radius, for modeling traffic lines, pipes or slender radiators. Types are Flow (volume flow rate per unit length and phase), Intensity or Power (free-space reference values at a distance) and User defined (monopole amplitude S). In Pressure Acoustics, Transient only Flow, User defined and Gaussian pulse are offered.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics > Edges > Line Source (als1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("als1", "FrequencyAcousticLineSource", 1)  (transient: "TransientAcousticLineSource")

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Flow (default) | Intensity | Power | UserDefined.

parameters.name: QsperLength, phi
parameters.description: Volume flow rate per unit length out from the source and phase.

parameters.name: I_rms / P_rms, dsrc
parameters.description: Free-space reference intensity or power and the distance from the source center.

parameters.name: S
parameters.description: Monopole amplitude (N/m^2) for the user-defined type.

tools.notes: Line Source on Axis is the 2D axisymmetric counterpart; in 2D the in-plane Monopole Point Source already represents an infinite line source.

tools.name: Line Source on Axis (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: Line source placed on the symmetry axis (r = 0) of a 2D axisymmetric component, representing a pulsating thin cylinder along the axis. It offers the same Flow, Intensity, Power and User defined types as the 3D Line Source, and Gaussian pulse in Pressure Acoustics, Transient. Useful for sources along the axis of horns, pipes or towed arrays modeled axisymmetrically.
tools.usage: 2D axisymmetric: right-click Pressure Acoustics > Edges > Line Source on Axis (aas1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("aas1", "FrequencyAcousticAxiSource", 1)  (transient: "TransientAcousticAxiSource")

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Flow (default) | Intensity | Power | UserDefined (GaussianPulse in transient).

parameters.name: QsperLength, phi, S
parameters.description: Flow per unit length, phase or monopole amplitude.

tools.notes: Only applicable to edges on the axis of symmetry.

tools.name: Circular Source (Pressure Acoustics, 2D Axisymmetric)
tools.description: Source applied at a point off the symmetry axis in a 2D axisymmetric component, which corresponds to a ring source in 3D; often used to mimic rotor or fan tonal sources in axisymmetric duct models. Types are Flow (volume flow rate per unit length and phase) or User defined, plus Gaussian pulse in Pressure Acoustics, Transient.
tools.usage: 2D axisymmetric: right-click Pressure Acoustics > Points > Circular Source (acs1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("acs1", "FrequencyAcousticCircularSource", 0)  (transient: "TransientAcousticCircularSource")

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Flow (default) | UserDefined.

parameters.name: QsperLength, phi
parameters.description: Volume flow rate per unit length (m^2/s) and phase.

parameters.name: S
parameters.description: Monopole amplitude for the user-defined type.

tools.notes: Combine with a nonzero azimuthal mode number in the interface settings to model spinning modes.

tools.name: Point Sources for 2D Components (Pressure Acoustics)
tools.description: In plane 2D components the monopole, dipole and quadrupole point sources represent infinite line sources in the out-of-plane direction: a pulsating cylinder, a cylinder oscillating back and forth, and two close opposite dipoles. The monopole has Flow, Intensity, Power and User defined types; amplitudes are per unit length (S in N/m, D in N/m). These are the 2D types behind the Points submenu of Pressure Acoustics.
tools.usage: 2D: right-click Pressure Acoustics > Points > Monopole/Dipole/Quadrupole Point Source. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("acpr").create("mls1", "FrequencyMonopoleLineSource", 0)  (also "FrequencyDipoleLineSource", "FrequencyQuadrupoleLineSource"; transient "TransientMonopoleLineSource")

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Flow (default) | Intensity | Power | UserDefined for the monopole.

parameters.name: QsperLength, phi
parameters.description: Volume flow rate per unit length and phase (Flow type).

parameters.name: I_rms / P_rms, dsrc
parameters.description: Free-space reference intensity/power and distance.

parameters.name: S
parameters.description: Monopole amplitude per unit length (user defined).

tools.notes: In 3D and 2D axisymmetry use FrequencyMonopolePointSource / FrequencyDipolePointSource (existing catalog entry 'Monopole Point Source / Dipole Point Source'). The transient 2D monopole supports the Gaussian pulse type (gaussian_explosion tutorial).

tools.name: Transient Pressure Acoustics Model (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Default domain node of Pressure Acoustics, Transient (actd) that solves the scalar wave equation for arbitrary time-dependent signals, with speed of sound and density allowed to vary slowly in space. Fluid models are Linear elastic, Viscous, Thermally conducting, Thermally conducting and viscous, General dissipation and Ideal gas; porous losses in the time domain need the Poroacoustics (rational approximation) node, and nonlinear propagation the Westervelt contributions. The interface also supports time-domain PMLs.
tools.usage: Pressure Acoustics, Transient > Transient Pressure Acoustics Model 1 (tpam1, default); set the maximum frequency to resolve in the interface Transient Solver Settings. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("actd", "TransientPressureAcoustics", "geom1"); physics("actd").feature("tpam1").set("FluidModel", "GeneralDissipation")

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: LinearElastic | Viscous | Thermal | Viscothermal | GeneralDissipation | IdealGas.

parameters.name: LinearElasticOption, c, rho, K_eff
parameters.description: crho | Krho specification of the lossless fluid.

parameters.name: delta_diff, mu, muB, kcond, Cp, gamma
parameters.description: Loss parameters of the dissipative models.

parameters.name: Maximum frequency to resolve (interface level)
parameters.description: Used to set the physics-controlled mesh and time step.

tools.notes: Resolve the shortest wavelength with about 5-6 second-order elements and use a time step of roughly 1/(60 fmax) with the generalized-alpha solver. For large domains with many wavelengths the dG-based Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit interface is more efficient.

tools.name: Nonlinear Acoustics (Westervelt) Contributions (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Domain subnode that turns the linear transient wave equation into the Westervelt equation, adding the cumulative nonlinear term governed by the coefficient of nonlinearity beta, to model finite-amplitude propagation, harmonic generation and shock formation (e.g. HIFU, high-intensity sirens). Linear acoustics is reasonable when the pressure is well below rho*c^2/beta (about 1.5e5 Pa in air, 2e9 Pa in water). Dissipation is added through the General dissipation fluid model; q-Laplacian relaxation can stabilize shocks.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Transient > Nonlinear Acoustics (Westervelt) Contributions (nlaw1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("actd").create("nlaw1", "NonlinearAcousticsWestervelt", 1)

parameters.name: MaterialDataOption
parameters.description: BA (parameter of nonlinearity B/A) | gamma (ideal gas) | beta (coefficient of nonlinearity).

parameters.name: BA, beta, gamma
parameters.description: Nonlinearity material data.

parameters.name: qLaplacianRelaxation, kappa, q
parameters.description: Enable q-Laplacian relaxation (shock capturing) with factor and exponent.

tools.notes: The equation is nonlinear: no superposition, and a Background Pressure Field cannot be used. Resolve the higher harmonics in mesh and time step. For large 3D nonlinear ultrasound use Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit.

tools.name: Background Pressure Field (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Defines a background (incident) pressure wave in the time domain so that the interface solves for the scattered field ps = pt - pb (scattered-field formulation). Field types are a monochromatic plane wave, a modulated Gaussian pulse (with bandwidth given as FWHM/FDHM of power or amplitude, or standard deviation) or a user-defined field; continuity of the total field is applied automatically where the background field is not defined on all domains. Combine with PMLs or radiation conditions for transient scattering.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Transient > Background Pressure Field (bpf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("actd").create("bpf1", "BackgroundPressureField", 3)

parameters.name: PressureFieldType
parameters.description: PlaneWave (monochromatic) | ModulatedGaussian | UserDefined.

parameters.name: pamp, c, dir, f0, phi
parameters.description: Amplitude, speed of sound, wave direction, signal frequency and phase.

parameters.name: x0, PulseBandwidth, df/dT/sigma
parameters.description: Signal emitting plane coordinate and pulse bandwidth definition for the Gaussian pulse.

parameters.name: UseRamp
parameters.description: Smoothly ramp the monochromatic wave in time.

parameters.name: p, u
parameters.description: User-defined background pressure and velocity fields.

tools.notes: Use with Exterior Field Calculation plus a Time to Frequency FFT study to obtain scattering patterns from a transient run. Not compatible with the Westervelt contributions.

tools.name: Impedance (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Time-domain impedance boundary condition for locally reacting surfaces, including frequency-dependent impedance through the General local reacting (rational approximation) option: measured or simulated admittance data are fitted by a Partial Fraction Fit function and converted to memory equations. Built-in options also include user-defined Zn and RCL-type lumped models (resistance, inertance, compliance). With Zn = rho*c it is the simplest absorbing boundary.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Transient > Impedance (imp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("actd").create("imp1", "Impedance", 2)

parameters.name: ImpedanceModel
parameters.description: UserDefined | RationalApproximation (plus RCL options in the GUI list).

parameters.name: Zn
parameters.description: Specific impedance (Pa*s/m) for the user-defined option.

parameters.name: ApproximantSource, ApproximantFunctionReference
parameters.description: UserDefined poles/residues or Function (a Partial Fraction Fit node).

parameters.name: Y_inf, Q, R, zeta, xi, ScaledPolesAndResidues
parameters.description: Asymptotic admittance, residues and poles of the rational approximation.

parameters.name: Rac, Lac, Cac, RCLModel
parameters.description: Lumped acoustic resistance, inertance, compliance and circuit topology.

tools.notes: The fitted admittance must be causal, real and passive. The same condition exists in Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit (wave_based_room uses it for carpet and ceiling data). The func() location of the Partial Fraction Fit (global or component) may differ in your model.

tools.name: Poroacoustics (Pressure Acoustics, Transient and Time Explicit)
tools.description: Time-domain equivalent-fluid model for porous materials: the frequency-dependent compressibility and density are represented by rational approximations (partial fraction expansions) whose inverse Fourier transform yields auxiliary memory equations solved in the porous domain. The fit is computed automatically for the Johnson-Champoux-Allard (JCA) and JCA-Lafarge (JCAL) models from the usual porous parameters, or taken from user-defined poles/residues or Partial Fraction Fit functions of measured data.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Transient (or Time Explicit) > Poroacoustics (pom1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pate").create("pom1", "TransientPoroacousticsModel", 3)

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: JohnsonChampouxAllard (default) | JohnsonChampouxAllardLafarge | UserDefined.

parameters.name: Rf, epsilon_p, tau, Lv, Lth, kp0_th
parameters.description: Porous matrix parameters for JCA/JCAL.

parameters.name: DensityApproximantSource / CompressibilityApproximantSource
parameters.description: UserDefined poles and residues or Function (Partial Fraction Fit) for density and compressibility.

parameters.name: rho_asymp, beta_asymp
parameters.description: Frequency-independent (asymptotic) density and compressibility.

tools.notes: The approximation must be (re)computed after changing porous parameters (a Compute button in the settings). Frequency-domain porous models are covered by Poroacoustics (Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain).

tools.name: Gaussian Pulse Source Type (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Predefined source time profile available as Type = Gaussian pulse for the Monopole Point Source, Line Source, Line Source on Axis, 2D point sources and Circular Source in Pressure Acoustics, Transient. The pulse is defined by its amplitude A, frequency bandwidth f0 and pulse peak time tp, producing a broadband impulse whose spectrum is controlled so the mesh can resolve it. Typical uses are impulse responses of rooms or explosions.
tools.usage: Pressure Acoustics, Transient > Monopole Point Source (or Line/Circular Source) > Type = Gaussian pulse. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("actd").create("mps1", "TransientMonopolePointSource", 0); feature("mps1").set("Type", "GaussianPulse")

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Flow | GaussianPulse | UserDefined.

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Pulse amplitude (m^3/s for point sources in 3D/axi, m^2/s for line-type sources).

parameters.name: f0
parameters.description: Frequency bandwidth of the pulse (Hz).

parameters.name: tp
parameters.description: Pulse peak time (s).

tools.notes: The Gaussian pulse type has no effect in the frequency domain. Set the interface's maximum frequency to resolve to about 2-3 times f0.

tools.name: Exterior Field Calculation (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Time-domain version of the Exterior Field Calculation: it defines the Helmholtz-Kirchhoff integral variables for the near and far field outside the computational domain, but they only produce results after the transient solution has been transformed to the frequency domain with a Time to Frequency FFT study step. It operates on the scattered field, so it is especially suited for scattering set up with a Background Pressure Field and a PML or radiation condition, or for radiation patterns of transient loudspeaker models.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Transient > Exterior Field Calculation (efc1); add Study > Time to Frequency FFT after the Time Dependent step. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("actd").create("efc1", "ExteriorFieldCalculation", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Closed surface enclosing all sources (inside any PML).

parameters.name: IntType, SymmetryType, SymmetryCondition0/1, ReflectionPlane
parameters.description: FullIntegral | IntegralApproximation (far-field limit), symmetry planes or sector symmetry and infinite-baffle (reflection plane) settings.

parameters.name: TimeToFreqFFT: fftmaxfreq, fftstarttime, fftendtime
parameters.description: FFT study settings that generate the frequency data.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. For frequency-domain models see the existing 'Exterior Field Calculation' entry; acpr.efc1.P_rad gives the radiated power there.

tools.name: Perfectly Matched Layer (Pressure Acoustics, Transient)
tools.description: Pressure Acoustics, Transient is the only transient acoustics interface that supports perfectly matched layers: in the PML domains COMSOL solves additional auxiliary equations obtained from the inverse Laplace transform of the complex coordinate stretching, giving an absorbing layer for all wave types and angles. The PML is defined under Definitions and applies automatically to actd; auxiliary variables such as actd.tpam1.pmlU appear in the solution.
tools.usage: Definitions > Perfectly Matched Layer (pml1) on the outer layer domains of a Pressure Acoustics, Transient model. Java: model.component("comp1").coordSystem().create("pml1", "PML"); model.component("comp1").coordSystem("pml1").selection().named("pml_domains")

parameters.name: Geometry type
parameters.description: Cartesian, cylindrical, spherical or user defined layer geometry.

parameters.name: Coordinate stretching type
parameters.description: Polynomial or rational stretching with scaling factor and curvature parameter.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: Use a swept mesh with about 8 layers through the PML.

tools.notes: Other transient interfaces (Thermoviscous Acoustics, Transient; Linearized Euler/Navier-Stokes, Transient; time-explicit dG interfaces) use absorbing layers or impedance conditions instead. PML properties (completion data): ScalingType = Cartesian | Cylindrical | Spherical | userDefined (per space dimension), stretchingType = polynomial | rational | userDefined, PMLfactor, PMLgamma, typicalWavelength.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model (Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Default domain node of Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit (pate), which solves the linearized continuity and momentum equations (quiescent linearized Euler) for pressure and particle velocity with the discontinuous Galerkin (dG-FEM) method and an explicit time stepper. The method is memory lean and suited for large transient problems spanning many wavelengths, such as wave-based room acoustics or ultrasound, and supports lossy fluid models, a Lax-Friedrichs flux parameter and an optional filter for stabilization.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit; node Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit Model 1 (patem1); Study > Time Dependent. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("pate", "PressureAcousticsTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: FluidModel
parameters.description: LinearElastic | Viscous | Thermal | Viscothermal | GeneralDissipation | IdealGas.

parameters.name: c, rho, K_eff
parameters.description: Fluid properties (crho or Krho specification).

parameters.name: LFtau
parameters.description: Lax-Friedrichs flux parameter (upwinding) of the dG flux.

parameters.name: ActivateFilter
parameters.description: Activate the spectral filter for stabilization.

parameters.name: Maximum frequency / use accelerated solver formulation (interface)
parameters.description: Mesh and time-step control; the accelerated formulation disables some features.

tools.notes: Use a mesh of quadratic or quartic dG elements with element size about lambda_min/1.5 for quartic order; the time step is set automatically from the CFL condition. Postprocessing variables include pate.p_t and pate.v_inst. Absorbing Layers (Definitions) replace PMLs.

tools.name: Background Acoustic Field (Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Sets up a background acoustic field (pressure pb and velocity ub) in the time-explicit dG interface so that the scattered fields ps and us are solved for. Field types are a monochromatic plane wave, a modulated Gaussian pulse or a user-defined pressure/velocity pair; total-field continuity is enforced automatically at domains without the background field. Used for transient scattering, e.g. an ultrasound pulse hitting a target.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit > Background Acoustic Field (baf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pate").create("baf1", "BackgroundAcousticFields", 3)

parameters.name: PressureFieldType
parameters.description: PlaneWave | ModulatedGaussian | UserDefined.

parameters.name: pamp, c, rho, dir, f0, phi
parameters.description: Amplitude, material, direction, signal frequency and phase.

parameters.name: x0, PulseBandwidth, df/dT/sigma, UseRamp
parameters.description: Pulse position and bandwidth definition, ramp option.

parameters.name: p, u
parameters.description: User-defined background pressure and velocity.

tools.notes: Not available when 'Use accelerated solver formulation' is enabled. Use Material Discontinuity at interfaces between different fluids.

tools.name: Mass Source / Volume Force Source / Heat Source (Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Domain sources of the time-explicit dG pressure acoustics interface: the Mass Source adds a mass rate of change M (kg/(m^3*s)) to the continuity equation (monopole-like), the Volume Force Source adds a force density F (N/m^3) to the momentum equation (dipole-like), and the Heat Source adds a thermal-expansion monopole. They correspond to the Monopole and Dipole Domain Sources of the FEM interfaces and are used for distributed transient excitation.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit > Mass Source (ms1) / Volume Force Source (vfs1) / Heat Source (hs1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pate").create("ms1", "MassSource", 3); create("vfs1", "VolumeForceSource", 3); create("hs1", "HeatSource", 3)

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Mass source (kg/(m^3*s)).

parameters.name: F
parameters.description: Volume force source vector (N/m^3).

parameters.name: Heat source
parameters.description: Heat power density with fluid thermal properties.

tools.notes: Not available with the accelerated solver formulation. Property names M and F are taken from the settings window symbols; verify with properties(). The same source types exist in Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit (nate).

tools.name: Impedance (Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Locally reacting impedance condition of the dG time-explicit interface relating total pressure and normal velocity through the specific acoustic impedance Zn; its default Zn = rho*c is the simplest nonreflecting condition. Frequency-dependent wall treatments (carpet, ceiling tiles, absorbers) are modeled with the General local reacting (rational approximation) option fed by a Partial Fraction Fit of measured admittance, and RCL lumped models are also available.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit > Impedance (imp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pate").create("imp1", "Impedance", 2)

parameters.name: ImpedanceModel
parameters.description: UserDefined (Zn) | RationalApproximation; RCLModel selects lumped circuit topologies.

parameters.name: ApproximantSource, ApproximantFunctionReference
parameters.description: Poles/residues entered by hand or taken from a Partial Fraction Fit function.

parameters.name: Zn
parameters.description: Specific acoustic impedance (default rho*c).

parameters.name: Rac, Lac, Cac, Area
parameters.description: Lumped RCL parameters and area.

tools.notes: Completion data lists ImpedanceModel = UserDefined | RationalApproximation (GUI: General local reacting (rational approximation)) for both pate and actd, plus RCLModel topologies (SerialRCL, ParallelRCL, ...). The fitted admittance must be causal, real and passive.

tools.name: Material Discontinuity / Continuity of Total Fields (Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit)
tools.description: Interior conditions specific to the discontinuous Galerkin formulation. Material Discontinuity must be applied where the characteristic impedance rho*c jumps (e.g. water/tissue or air/porous interfaces) to enforce continuity of total pressure and normal velocity correctly. Continuity of Total Fields is a default node that activates automatically when a Background Acoustic Field or Poroacoustics is applied on only part of the domains.
tools.usage: Right-click Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit > Interior Conditions > Material Discontinuity (md1); Continuity of Total Fields (tfc1) is added by default. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pate").create("md1", "MaterialDiscontinuity", 2)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Interior boundaries between domains with different materials.

tools.notes: Both nodes are unavailable with the accelerated solver formulation. Elastic Waves, Time Explicit and Nonlinear Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit have their own Material Discontinuity nodes (hifu_tissue_sample uses one).

tools.name: Scattering Object (Pressure Acoustics, Asymptotic Scattering)
tools.description: Singleton node of the Asymptotic Scattering interface that selects the domains or finite voids forming the scattering object(s); its Wall subnodes define the surface reflection properties. Wall types are Sound hard wall (R = 1), Reflection coefficient R, Normal impedance Zn (locally reacting, converted with the plane-wave reflection formula) or Absorption coefficient with phase; R and alpha may depend on the local angle of incidence through paas.theta or paas.costheta.
tools.usage: Pressure Acoustics, Asymptotic Scattering > Scattering Object 1 (so1, default) > Wall 1 (wall1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("paas").feature("so1").feature("wall1").set("Type", "NormalImpedance")

parameters.name: Selection (so1)
parameters.description: Domains/finite voids forming the scatterer.

parameters.name: Type (wall)
parameters.description: Sound hard wall (default) | Reflection coefficient | Normal impedance | Absorption coefficient.

parameters.name: R, Zn, alpha, phi
parameters.description: Reflection coefficient, normal impedance (Pa*s/m), absorption coefficient and phase.

tools.notes: Secondary scattering between disconnected objects is not included. Type = AbsorptionCoefficient with an interpolation function alpha(paas.theta) is used in the submarine tutorial; other Type tokens follow the same CamelCase naming (check with getString("Type")).

tools.name: Radiating Object (Pressure Acoustics, Kirchhoff-Helmholtz)
tools.description: Singleton node of the Kirchhoff-Helmholtz interface that selects the domains or finite voids of the vibrating body; its Wall subnodes define the surface source. Wall types are Velocity (surface velocity vector, e.g. solid.u_tX, solid.u_tY, solid.u_tZ from a Solid Mechanics solution), Normal velocity (pointing into the fluid) or User defined (both p and vn, full control of the Kirchhoff-Helmholtz integral). Scattering by the object itself is not taken into account.
tools.usage: Pressure Acoustics, Kirchhoff-Helmholtz > Radiating Object 1 (ro1, default) > Wall 1. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("pakh").feature("ro1").feature("wall1").set("vn", "vn_hull")

parameters.name: Selection (ro1)
parameters.description: Domains/finite voids of the radiating body.

parameters.name: Type (wall)
parameters.description: Velocity (default) | Normal velocity | User defined.

parameters.name: v, vn, p
parameters.description: Surface velocity vector, normal velocity (m/s) or user-defined pressure and normal velocity.

tools.notes: Tags ro1/wall1 follow the default naming (RadiatingObject id 'ro'); property names v/vn/p follow the settings window symbols and should be verified with properties().
